Next is the procedures file. Three Oracle behaviours don't carry over directly, so I'm handling them as follows:

- `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` can't run inside a block that has an `EXCEPTION` clause, and `COMMIT` breaks when the caller already has a transaction open. I'll drop both and let the caller own the transaction. An error in `sp_monthly_report` still rolls back its own work, because the `EXCEPTION` block runs as a subtransaction.
- `FROM DUAL` and `%ROWTYPE` have no direct equivalent, so the row count becomes a constant and the row variable goes away.
- The custom `e_no_data` exception becomes a `P0002` SQLSTATE, which Postgres maps to `no_data_found`.

-- ============================================================================
-- PostgreSQL procedures — converted from the Oracle PL/SQL in oracle/*.sql
--
-- Notes on the conversion:
--   * sysdate            -> now()
--   * NVL(a, b)          -> COALESCE(a, b)
--   * VARCHAR2(n)        -> varchar(n)
--   * %TYPE / %ROWTYPE   -> explicit column types / no row variable needed
--   * DUAL               -> the constant 1 (a single-row source), which is
--                           exactly what Oracle's SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DUAL gave
--   * COMMIT / ROLLBACK  -> removed. Transaction control belongs to the caller
--                           (CALL runs in autocommit unless wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT).
--                           A COMMIT inside a block with an EXCEPTION clause is
--                           not allowed in PostgreSQL, and the EXCEPTION block
--                           already rolls back its own work on error.
--   * user-defined exception e_no_data -> RAISE with SQLSTATE 'P0002'
--                           (no_data_found), caught by the handler below.
-- ============================================================================

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_customer_tier: per-customer spend tiers from orders
--   GOLD >= 1000, SILVER >= 500, otherwise BRONZE
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_customer_tier()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    rec       RECORD;
    v_tier    varchar(20);
    v_status  varchar(20);
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM customer_tiers;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT o.customer_id,
               c.customer_name,
               SUM(o.order_total) AS total_spend,
               COUNT(*)           AS order_count
        FROM   orders o
        JOIN   customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
        WHERE  COALESCE(c.status, 'ACTIVE') = 'ACTIVE'
        GROUP  BY o.customer_id, c.customer_name
    LOOP
        IF rec.total_spend >= 1000 THEN
            v_tier := 'GOLD';
        ELSIF rec.total_spend >= 500 THEN
            v_tier := 'SILVER';
        ELSE
            v_tier := 'BRONZE';
        END IF;

        INSERT INTO customer_tiers
            (customer_id, customer_name, total_spend, order_count, tier, computed_at)
        VALUES
            (rec.customer_id, rec.customer_name, rec.total_spend, rec.order_count,
             v_tier, now());
    END LOOP;

    -- Mirrors the Oracle "SELECT status INTO v_status ... WHERE ROWNUM = 1":
    -- raises no_data_found when customers is empty, as Oracle did.
    SELECT status INTO STRICT v_status FROM customers LIMIT 1;
END;
$$;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_monthly_report(p_month): revenue and units per product category
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_monthly_report(p_month IN varchar)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    rec        RECORD;
    v_has_data numeric := 0;
BEGIN
    -- Oracle: SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_has_data FROM DUAL;  (always 1)
    v_has_data := 1;

    DELETE FROM monthly_report WHERE report_month = p_month;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT p.category                                 AS category,
               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) AS revenue,
               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0)              AS units_sold
        FROM   order_items oi
        JOIN   products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
        GROUP  BY p.category
    LOOP
        INSERT INTO monthly_report
            (report_month, category, revenue, units_sold)
        VALUES
            (p_month, rec.category, rec.revenue, rec.units_sold);
    END LOOP;

    IF v_has_data = 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'no data for report month %', p_month
            USING ERRCODE = 'P0002';
    END IF;
EXCEPTION
    -- Oracle "WHEN e_no_data THEN ROLLBACK;". The EXCEPTION block is a
    -- subtransaction, so the DELETE/INSERTs above are already undone here.
    WHEN no_data_found THEN
        NULL;
    -- Oracle "WHEN OTHERS THEN ROLLBACK; RAISE;"
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE;
END;
$$;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_customer_tier: per-customer spend tiers from orders
--   GOLD >= 1000, SILVER >= 500, otherwise BRONZE
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_customer_tier()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    rec       RECORD;
    v_tier    varchar(20);
    v_status  varchar(20);
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM customer_tiers;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT o.customer_id,
               c.customer_name,
               SUM(o.order_total) AS total_spend,
               COUNT(*)           AS order_count
        FROM   orders o
        JOIN   customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
        WHERE  COALESCE(c.status, 'ACTIVE') = 'ACTIVE'
        GROUP  BY o.customer_id, c.customer_name
    LOOP

            v_tier := 'GOLD';
        ELSIF rec.total_spend >= 500 THEN
            v_tier := 'SILVER';
        ELSE
            v_tier := 'BRONZE';

               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0)              AS units_sold
        FROM   order_items oi
        JOIN   products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
        GROUP  BY p.category
    LOOP
